item.title: Shortest Synchronizing Words on Product Automata
item.description: arXiv:2611.09136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider some operations on finite automata graphs, in particular various product, union and merge operations, and investigate how they relate to the parameter~$\mathrm{rt}$, the \emph{length of a shortest synchronizing word}. We derive some lower and upper bounds for the operations that we study. We also examine several classes of automata (for instance, partially ordered, commutative or idempotent automata) that are preserved under these operations and show in which way the parameter $\mathrm{rt}$ behaves in these automata classes. Also, we consider automata classes that can be constructed by combining automata from better known classes; in particular, these new classes of automata will also satisfy the bound of the famous \v{C}ern\'y conjecture. This also motivates us to study even more closure properties. In particular, we show that certain automata classes related to synchronization form pseudo-varieties. We also commence a similar study concerning the length of shortest homing sequences of Mealy automata.
item.dc:creator: Henning Fernau, Igor Rystsov

item.title: Word Subtraction Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.09157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note is a self-contained text on word subtraction games, combinatorial games in which players alternately remove a nonempty suffix belonging to a prescribed subtraction set from the current word. It collects and develops basic results on these games from the viewpoints of combinatorial game theory and formal language theory. We focus on the relationship between subtraction sets and the resulting languages of winning and losing positions. The topics include finite, regular, and context-free subtraction sets, as well as several variants and further developments.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Inoue, Hiroki Inazu

item.title: Fast and General Automatic Differentiation for Finite-State Methods
item.description: arXiv:2602.12300v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a new method, that we coined the ``morphism-trick'', to integrate custom implementations of vector-Jacobian products in automatic differentiation softwares, applicable to a wide range of semiring-based computations. Our approach leads to efficient and semiring-agnostic implementations of the backward pass of dynamic programming algorithms. For the particular case of finite-state methods, we introduce an algorithm that computes and differentiates the $\oplus$-sum of all paths' weight of a finite-state automaton. Results show that, with minimal effort from the user, our novel library allows computing the gradient of a function w.r.t. to the weights of a finite state automaton orders of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art automatic differentiation systems. Implementations are made available via an open-source library distributed under a permissive license.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ondel Yang (LISN, CNRS), Caio Corro (INSA Rennes, IRISA, ARCHIMEDIA), Nicolas Denier (LISN), Martin Kocour (FIT / BUT, BUT), Tina Raissi (RWTH Aachen), Pablo Riera (ICC)

item.title: A quadratic lower bound for 2DFAs against one-way liveness
item.description: arXiv:2602.24279v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that every two-way deterministic finite automaton (2DFA) that solves one-way liveness on height h has Omega(h^2) states. This implies a quadratic lower bound for converting one-way nondeterministic finite automata to 2DFAs, which asymptotically matches Chrobak's well-known lower bound for this conversion on unary languages. In contrast to Chrobak's simple proof, which relies on a 2DFA's inability to differentiate between any two sufficiently distant locations in a unary input, our argument can be applied to inputs over any alphabet and is structured around a main lemma that is general enough to potentially be reused elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: Kehinde Adeogun, Christos Kapoutsis

item.title: Approximating the Reachability Value of Posterior-Deterministic POMDPs
item.description: arXiv:2602.07473v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce posterior-deterministic POMDPs, and we show that for this class of POMDPs, the maximal probability of reaching a given set of states can be approximated up to arbitrary precision. A POMDP is posterior-deterministic if the next state can be uniquely determined by the current state, the action taken, and the observation received. In particular, once the current state is known, it remains known forever. The class contains, for instance, multiple-environment MDPs equipped with a prior distribution over the environments, quasi-deterministic POMDPs, and the episodic version of the classical Tiger POMDP (Kaelbling et al. 1998).
item.dc:creator: Nathana\"el Fijalkow, Arka Ghosh, Roman Kniazev, Guillermo A. P\'erez, Pierre Vandenhove
